question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $7$ modulo $12,$ denoted ${7}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
7\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,12).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(7,12)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $12.$

Since the modulus $n=12$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $7$ (modulo $12$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{2} & ≡7\cdot 7≡49≡4\cdot 12+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $7\cdot 7≡1\,(\text{mod}\,12).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $7$ modulo $12$ is $7.$
